children: rose 2.2% in Friday's trading as Raymond James raised its rating to Market Outperform from Market Perform with a $32 price target, saying its recent selloff following the Chevron
restructuring has created an attractive entry point for investors.
The Bakken contract reset was severe, reducing estimated 2027 EBITDA by $400M while pausing distribution growth and increasing leverage, yet Chevron's
~38% ownership cancellation, contribution of D-J Basin assets, and contract extensions to 2045 provide Hess Midstream
with a meaningful exchange of value for the lower rates, Raymond James analyst J.R. Weston said.
The pause in 2027 distribution growth has weighted on Hess Midstream

sentiment, but the payout looks supported by $525M-$625M of guided adjusted free cash flow against $420M-$425M of distribution, which Weston said should allow leverage to move from 3.75x-4x to the 3.5x-3.75x longer-term target through 2029.
While fixed reservation payments expire after 2029, the analyst expects the existing payout to remain covered via retained free cash flow, modest D-J growth, and potential operating efficiencies.
"All in, risk is overstated and growth upside is feasible (though not necessary)," Weston wrote.

title: Hess Midstream upgraded at Raymond James as Chevron restructuring selloff overdone
